title: Operator upgrade fencing and manifest checksum audit to prevent partial on-prem tenant upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers in the Private/VPC tier reported tenant workloads entering a degraded state during operator-led platform upgrades. Root cause analysis points to a race between operator reconciliation and Helm post-upgrade hooks: when leader handoff or controller restarts happen mid-rollout, some tenant CRs are partially applied and node-level readiness (NODEREADY) or APIServer transient errors lead to manifests being accepted by the cluster but not reconciled by the operator, leaving tenants with a mix of new/old resources. This ticket implements a multi-pronged fix: (1) introduce an operator-side upgrade fencing mechanism (upgrade lock with TTL and owner identity) to ensure only one controller instance performs cluster-wide upgrade reconciliation, (2) compute and store manifest checksums in the Helm release CR (and operator state) so we can detect partial application and trigger safe rollbacks or retries, and (3) add an emergency image-pin fallback and staged rollout mode to limit blast radius. Work includes implementing the operator changes, helm chart adjustments, e2e tests that simulate controller preemption, and updating the runbook and customer-facing rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: Operator exposes an upgrade fencing lock with owner identity and TTL that prevents concurrent cluster-wide reconciles
Manifest checksums are recorded for each tenant manifest and mismatches are detected during post-upgrade validation
On checksum mismatch the operator either safely retries or performs a deterministic rollback according to policy
Staged rollout mode can be toggled via release annotation and limits simultaneous tenant upgrades to a configurable batch size
Automated integration tests simulate controller failover and verify no tenant is left in a partially-upgraded state
Runbook updated with clear steps for engineers and customer success for manual remediation and for initiating emergency image pin fallback
implementation_notes: Add UpgradeFence type to operator control-plane config: owner_id, acquired_at, ttl_seconds, last_renewed
On reconcile start, operator attempts to acquire fence; if not owner, exit fast and requeue after jittered backoff
Calculate manifest checksum as sha256 over normalized YAML; store on HelmRelease CR annotation and operator status field
Post-helm-hook verification: operator compares applied manifests' checksums to expected; on mismatch run determinism checks and either retry helm upgrade or annotate release for rollback
Expose gated FeatureFlag 'stagedTenantRollout' behind operator config and console toggle; default off for early rollout
Add e2e scenario: simulate controller pod eviction during helm upgrade, assert no tenant resources remain in mixed-version state
Implementation should avoid global locks that prevent normal per-tenant reconciliation; fence is scoped to upgrade operations only
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/helm-charts/pull/98 - helm chart annotation for manifest checksum

notes_for_support: Temporary mitigation: instruct customer to enable 'helm.release.recreatePods' and run 'kubectl rollout restart' for the affected tenant namespace. For severe cases, follow the runbook to pin operator image to previous digest and trigger a safe retry via the operator CLI. Communicate ETA and monitor the upgrade-failures dashboard.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: fence TTL misconfiguration could block upgrades if operator fails to renew; mitigation: conservative default TTL (2m) and auto-release on controller restart plus emergency force-unlock CLI. Tests to cover TTL expiration and forced-unlock flows.
